practicalSkillsWorkflowAgreement: Use choreograph to write the causal sequence before editing: notice, read/consider, visitor return, one offered-hand turn and hold. Identify intentionally quiet channels and required contacts alongside moving channels.

Use animate and review-animations to review the displayed pose as well as the engine pose. Layout correction is a second state layer, so replay/resize/pause tests must exercise their handoff rather than only verify settled targets.

Use animation-performance to verify that layout reads stay outside the frame loop and that paused/reduced states have no independent clock. Diagnose any future cost with an attributed trace before changing properties or adding will-change.

Keep same-time before/current frames, actual-size day/night ladders and the destination composition together. A larger portrait improvement does not erase a compact-use deduction; purposeful chin and clasp contact are judged as relationships, not contour overlap counts.

Keep numeric bounds, rendered contact, callback cadence, continuous perception, physical devices and unfamiliar-human responses in separate evidence categories. The replay-envelope diagnostic belongs to the first category only.

Carry prior deductions forward with explicit resolution status, preserve hashes and independent scores, and give future engineers precise reproduction and acceptance criteria. B's additional design-engineering/audit skills support the same evidence workflow; my own full-skill intake remains the four animation skills recorded in the independent review.

Required chin/clasp contact is not removed to satisfy a generic separation rule. A completely still reduced-motion pose and frozen paused resize are valid here.
